steps.what: Advise customers concerning equipment operation, maintenance and programming

tasks.design: Retain direct advice and demonstration by the repair technician. Approved instructions in {DOCS} support the discussion without assuming that customer understanding takes less time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice depends on the installed configuration and the customer's experience.
tasks.enabler_now: Accessible manuals support explanations but do not establish shorter teaching sessions.
tasks.human_edge: The technician demonstrates and adapts advice to observed use.
tasks.altitude: No change to advice time or responsibility.

reach.task: Coordinate user guidance for connected equipment

evidence.claim: Equipment advice often requires contextual demonstration and checking understanding; this decomposition claims no software labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is customer advice, excluding separate repair records and manual publication.
Technician observes the equipment and asks questions during the unchanged full-time conversation; no free structured configuration feed is assumed.
Use existing approved manuals before adding an answer tool.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new service is introduced.
research_questions: Which advice delays are manual lookup rather than necessary explanation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0. The customer conversation remains unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check parts inventories and capture counts, usage and repair needs
Calculate replenishment quantities and prepare additional parts orders
Resolve stock exceptions and authorise the parts order

tasks.design: Configure replenishment drafts from the {OTHER} field-service inventory and supplier data in {PROCUREMENT}. The technician still counts stock, confirms repair needs and releases the exact order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock observations and reorder calculations are handled separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Native stock rules can calculate draft quantities from checked inputs.
tasks.still_hard: Substitutions, obsolete parts and uncertain urgent demand.
tasks.human_edge: The technician checks compatibility and repair urgency.
tasks.altitude: Less calculation and order preparation with purchasing decisions unchanged.

evidence.claim: FieldBuddy provides asset management and technician work-order checklists. The replenishment formula and time saving here remain E1 design assumptions.
Checked stock quantities, outstanding orders and explicit reorder rules can create a parts-order draft deterministically.

assumptions: Boundary covers local stock checks and order preparation/release, excluding supplier picking and delivery.

Technician produces part identifier, location, usable on-hand quantity, reserved quantity, repair need and count timestamp in s1. Its unchanged 45 hours include counting, usage capture and correction; no stock accuracy is assumed free.

Maintenance supervisor produces reorder point, target stock and approved substitutions; purchasing staff maintain supplier identifier, price and pack size. Added policy review costs two other-role hours per 100 focal baseline hours. s3 handles missing policy or uncertain compatibility manually.
Test native inventory rules first. Five focal upkeep hours cover count discrepancies and rule tests; existing runtime earns no saving.
research_questions: Do replenishment drafts remove preparation time after stock capture and exception checks?

incremental.description: Review stock discrepancies and test replenishment rules

approvals.approved_version: Exact supplier, part identifiers, quantities, prices, destination and order version; changes void authorisation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+0+25=70; gross 30 less 5 upkeep gives net 25. Low 8 allows 17 extra manual preparation hours for obsolete or irregular parts. Counting and release stay unchanged; E1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Converse with customers to determine details of equipment problems

tasks.design: Keep the diagnostic conversation with the repair technician. Existing incident information in {HELPDESK} can support questioning, but does not replace clarification of what the customer observed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customers describe symptoms imprecisely and omit context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing incident records support continuity without proving a shorter conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing symptoms, intermittent faults and user expectations.
tasks.human_edge: The technician asks targeted follow-up questions and notices contradictions.
tasks.altitude: No change to customer conversation time.

evidence.claim: A customer fault conversation requires contextual clarification; work-order drafting does not by itself shorten that conversation.

assumptions: Boundary is eliciting fault details, excluding recording the repair and performing diagnosis tests.
Customer supplies observations in conversation; technician clarifies them within the full-time step. No structured fault code or transcript is presumed.
Review native incident access first; no model service is introduced.
Zero incremental upkeep because the conversation remains unchanged.
research_questions: Which repeat questions reflect missing records rather than necessary clarification?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0. Customer clarification retains its full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Capture equipment maintenance work, parts and test observations
Transfer captured maintenance details into the asset service history
Check and save the final equipment maintenance record

tasks.design: Capture service facts once in the {OTHER} field-service form and populate the asset history from those fields. Keep technician capture and final factual review; no model is needed for repeated fields.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service notes are retyped into a separate asset history.
tasks.enabler_now: Native checklists and asset records can reuse one captured set of facts.
tasks.still_hard: Accurate fault descriptions and distinguishing work performed from recommendations.
tasks.human_edge: The technician knows what actually happened on the equipment.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated record entry while retaining accountability for service facts.

reach.learn: Consistent failure coding and history interpretation

evidence.claim: FieldBuddy provides technician checklists, work orders and asset management, supporting structured service recording.

assumptions: Boundary is record capture and maintenance, excluding actual repair, testing and separate invoicing.

Technician produces asset identifier, work-order identifier, date, fault, action performed, parts identifiers and quantities, hours, test values and unresolved issues in s1. Its full 45 hours include data entry, code selection and clarifying incomplete facts.
s2 copies only captured fields to a draft; missing asset matches or unsupported legacy records fall back to manual entry in s3 and reduce savings.
Test native asset-history reuse first. Five focal upkeep hours and two other-role mapping-support hours are additional per 100 baseline hours. Existing integrated runtime earns no saving.
research_questions: Can one structured capture eliminate repeated entry without adding form completion time?

already_counted.description: Check source facts and save final record

incremental.description: Review failed matches and maintain form fields

approvals.approved_version: Exact asset identifier, work-order identifier, performed actions, parts, hours and test values; edits void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+0+20=65; gross 35 minus 5 upkeep gives net 30. Low 10 allows 20 hours of manual legacy-record fallback. Capture and review retain all their time; E1 scenario.
